prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: square museum-quality painterly encyclopedia illustration for Mythics. Subject: ONE Hungarian SÁRKÁNY, specifically the tarajos kígyó / crested-serpent variant described in the Hungarian Ethnographic Lexicon: a dreadful winged, hard-scaled serpent, horse-like at the front and snake-like behind, long claws, long teeth, flaming crest, breathing sparks and flame. Show one elongated horse-like reptilian head, long fanged equine muzzle, scaled horse-like neck and chest; front has exactly TWO long-clawed forelegs; behind the chest is ONE long tapering limbless serpentine body and tail, no horse hindquarters and no hind legs. Exactly TWO broad membranous wings, with both wing bases visibly attached to the shoulders. A fiery red crest follows the head and upper neck; a short controlled stream of sparks exits the mouth. Full body three-quarter side view clearly shows the whole anatomy, poised in a rocky marsh clearing beneath thunderclouds, rain and distant lightning. Menacing primal supernatural storm aura, dark red hard scales with black accents, warm fire highlights against cold slate storm light. Detailed elegant painted realism, richly textured scales, mature mythological field-guide art. Constraints: one creature, one head, two wings, two forelegs, one continuous serpent tail; horse-like front must remain visibly nonhuman and reptilian. No rider, humans, humanoid torso, ordinary person, extra heads, horns, extra wings, extra limbs, text, border, logo or watermark. This is a researched folk variant, not a generic four-legged fantasy dragon.
